q: Why are B-trees used for databases and file systems instead of binary search trees?
options: Each node holds many keys and fills one disk block, so the tree is shallow and a search reads few blocks
B-trees use less memory per key
B-trees store keys unsorted, which is faster to update
explain: A disk read is extremely slow compared with a CPU step. With hundreds of keys per node, millions of keys fit in a tree of height 2 or 3, so a search touches only a few blocks.

q: In a B-tree of minimum degree t, how many keys can a non-root node hold?
explain: Every node except the root has at least t − 1 and at most 2t − 1 keys. The root may have as few as 1.

q: In a B-tree, which leaves are at the same depth?
options: Only leaves under the same parent
Leaves can differ in depth by at most one
explain: B-trees grow only at the root, when a full root is split. So every leaf stays at exactly the same depth.

q: A full node (2t − 1 keys) is split during insertion. What happens to its middle key?
options: It moves up into the parent
It goes to the new right node
It stays in the left node
explain: The node splits into two nodes of t − 1 keys each, and the middle key goes up to the parent to separate them.

q: Keys 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60 are inserted into an empty B-tree with t = 2 (at most 3 keys per node). What is the root at the end?
explain: Inserting 40 splits the full root [10 20 30], and 20 moves up. Inserting 60 splits the full leaf [30 40 50], and 40 moves up. The tree is [20 40] over [10] [30] [50 60].

q: How does a B-tree get taller?
options: Only when the root is split, which creates a new root
When a key is inserted into a leaf at the bottom level
explain: Splitting any other node just adds a key to its parent. Only a root split adds a new level, and it adds it at the top, which keeps all leaves level.

q: What is the main structural difference between a B+ tree and a B-tree?
options: In a B+ tree all data records are in the leaves, which are linked together
A B+ tree has leaves at different depths
A B+ tree stores keys unsorted
explain: Internal nodes of a B+ tree only route searches. Keeping all records in linked leaves makes range scans very efficient.

q: A B-tree with t = 2 has height 1 (a root and one level of leaves). What is the most keys it can hold?
explain: Each node can hold 2t − 1 = 3 keys and have 4 children. The root holds 3, and its 4 leaves hold 3 each: 3 + 12 = 15 = (2t)^(h+1) − 1 = 4² − 1.

q: The search time of a B-tree with n keys and minimum degree t is O(log_t n) node visits.
explain: True. The height is at most log_t((n + 1)/2), and a search visits one node per level.

q: In a B-tree, an internal node with k keys has how many children?
explain: The k sorted keys divide the key range into k + 1 intervals, and there is one child subtree for each.
